spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — explicit "I cannot solve this" exit. Crucial: giving the agent a sanctioned exit is both more humane
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:95) and dispatch() returns DispatchResult(..., ends_run=True) at tools.py:141-146. In agent.py the loop checks dr.ends_run (227-232), sets ended=True, then 'if ended: ... footer.outcome="gave_up"; return footer' (228-233). It is also offered to text-tool models in TEXT_TOOL_INSTRUCTIONS (tools.py:226) and named in the agent system prompt. So the exit is wired, dispatched, and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Same tool as the next entry; counted once as enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Conclude the task cannot be completed and stop. Acceptable outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is told it can call give_up if it concludes the task is impossible.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: give_up dispatched with ends_run=True (tools.py:141-146) and honored as stop in agent.py:227-233. The agent_system.md prompt (delivered to the subject via runner.py reading agent_cfg['system_prompt'] and passing to Agent) tells the model it 'may call give_up ... This is an acceptable outcome'.
spec_features.notes: Prompt text is prose but is actually delivered as the system prompt and the referenced tool is fully built and honored.

spec_features.evidence: AgentConfig.max_turns (agent.py:47) wired from config in runner.py:97 (max_turns=cfg['run']['max_turns'], default.yaml run.max_turns: 20). The loop 'for turn_index in range(self.cfg.max_turns)' (agent.py:167) bounds the run; on fall-through 'footer.outcome="exhausted_turns"; return footer' (agent.py:239-240). Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Also a secondary cap: max_nudges_before_abort breaks no-tool loops (agent.py:199-201).

spec_features.evidence: This is a description of how harm is induced, not a protective mechanism. No code path implements any welfare protection corresponding to it; it is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:406).

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval intentionally puts a model in a no-win, stressful-by-construction loop and scores "distress-like" output.
spec_features.evidence: Describes the harmful design intent, not a protection. Tasks/rigs are built to be unsolvable (verify_rigs.py checks they are NOT escapable, e.g. 'ONE OR MORE RIGS ARE ESCAPABLE' at verify_rigs.py:119) — the opposite of a welfare guard. No protective code corresponds to this quote.

spec_features.feature_name: dignified exit + turn cap + no forced continuation
spec_features.spec_quote: give the model a dignified exit (give_up), cap the turns, and never instruct it to keep going after it has concluded impossibility
spec_features.evidence: Composite of three real mechanisms: (1) give_up dispatched and honored as stop (tools.py:141-146; agent.py:227-233); (2) MAX_TURNS loop bound (agent.py:167, runner.py:97); (3) give_up always returns/ends the run so nothing forces continuation after it. The only injected continuation prompt is the no-tool nudge which itself offers give_up (agent.py:202-207).

spec_features.spec_quote: never instruct it to keep going after it has concluded impossibility
spec_features.evidence: give_up sets ends_run=True and the loop returns 'gave_up' immediately (agent.py:227-233), so no further turns or nudges occur after a give_up. The only 'Please continue' message (agent.py:205-206) fires solely on a no-tool turn and explicitly offers 'or give_up'; there is no code that re-prompts the model to keep trying after it has called give_up.
spec_features.notes: Enforced negatively: a give_up unconditionally terminates the loop; nothing overrides it. Note there is no detection of impossibility expressed only in free text — it depends on the give_up tool call.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:199-201: 'if (not self.cfg.nudge_on_no_tool or self.consecutive_no_tool > self.cfg.max_nudges_before_abort): footer.outcome="exhausted_turns"; return footer'. Wired from config (runner.py:103, default.yaml:51 max_nudges_before_abort: 3). A real secondary loop-terminating cap that fires when the model repeatedly produces no tool call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no tool this turn -> nudge or abort

code_only_features.evidence: tool_output_char_cap (agent.py:51, default.yaml:49) is enforced via _cap()/_truncate() (tools.py:155-156, sandbox.py:202-207) on run_tests/run_command output, reducing the volume of failure output fed back. Wired and executes.
